name: zapfast
description: ZapFast: a fast, native WhatsApp client in Rust and egui
readme_content:
ZapFast

WhatsApp, native and fast.
A lightweight WhatsApp app for Linux, macOS, and Windows.

Download · Getting started · User guide · Contribute

ZapFast is a WhatsApp client written in Rust with [egui](https://www.egui.rs) and [fastframe](https://fastframe.dev), the framework behind a family of native desktop apps. It links to your phone as a companion device through [whatsapp-rust](https://github.com/oxidezap/whatsapp-rust) and has no browser engine. In our Linux test it opens in under a second and uses about 200 MB of idle RAM, against 1.13 GB for WhatsApp Web. [See the measurements](https://zapfast.rocks/benchmarks/). The interface is available in English, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), French, German, Indonesian, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Spanish, and Turkish.
Watch ZapFast in action https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2bf86b54-45fc-4add-8de7-c426c3cdad9b
[Features](#your-chats-on-your-desktop) · [Install](#install) · [Link your phone](#link-your-phone) · [Help](#guides-and-help) ## Your chats, on your desktop | Feature | What you can do | |---|---| | **Messages** | Send formatted text, replies, edits, reactions, forwards, pictures, files, stickers, GIFs, polls, and voice messages. | | **Media in the chat** | Play voice messages, videos, round video messages, GIFs, and animated stickers in place. | | **Your history** | Keep your chats in an encrypted archive on this computer, fetch older messages from your phone as you scroll, and export locally saved chat history as text or a ZIP with downloaded attachments. | | **Several numbers** | Link more than one WhatsApp number and switch between them in one window. | | **Desktop controls** | Use keyboard shortcuts, select and copy text across messages, and stay linked in the tray with notifications. | | **Themes** | Choose light, dark, system appearance, or custom colours. On Omarchy, follow your desktop theme. | | **Privacy** | Hide locked chats behind a code, or the whole window behind an app lock. Nothing goes to a server of ours. | ## Install | Platform | Installation | |---|---| | **macOS** | `brew install --cask crmne/tap/zapfast`, or [download the Mac app](https://zapfast.rocks/download/#macos). | | **Arch Linux** | `yay -S zapfast-bin` | | **Windows** | Choose your build on the [Download page](https://zapfast.rocks/download/#windows). | | **Other Linux** | Find Nix, AppImage, and other options on the [Download page](https://zapfast.rocks/download/#linux). | | **From source** | Follow [Getting started](https://zapfast.rocks/getting-started/) for dependencies and commands. | ## Link your phone 1. Open ZapFast. It shows a QR code. 2. On your phone, open WhatsApp, then **Settings**, **Linked devices**, **Link a device**, and scan the code. Or click **Link with phone number** and enter the eight-character code on your phone. 3. Your recent chats arrive from the phone. Older messages follow as you scroll up. The link survives restarts, and your phone does not need to stay online to read what ZapFast has already stored. See [Getting started](https://zapfast.rocks/getting-started/) for the full walkthrough and [How it links](https://zapfast.rocks/how-it-links/) for the details. ## Guides and help The complete guide lives at **[zapfast.rocks](https://zapfast.rocks/)**. | You want to… | Read | |---|---| | Know what ZapFast does and does not do yet | [What is ZapFast?](https://zapfast.rocks/what-is-zapfast/) | | Link your phone or build from source | [Getting started](https://zapfast.rocks/getting-started/) | | Learn messages, stickers, polls, and shortcuts | [Using ZapFast](https://zapfast.rocks/using-zapfast/) | | Find settings, stored files, encryption, the app lock, and updates | [Settings and files](https://zapfast.rocks/settings-and-files/) | | Make your own theme | [Making a theme](https://zapfast.rocks/themes/) | | Understand what stays on this computer | [How it links](https://zapfast.rocks/how-it-links/) | | Understand account risk | [Account safety](https://zapfast.rocks/what-is-zapfast/#account-safety) | | Report a bug or propose a feature | Read [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md), then use the [issue forms](https://github.com/crmne/zapfast/issues/new/choose). | ## Contributing Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening an issue or pull request. To look at the interface without a WhatsApp account, run: ```sh cargo run --features demo -- --demo ``` [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) describes the architecture, [DEMO.md](DEMO.md) the demo pages, screenshots, and recorded tours, and [PACKAGING.md](PACKAGING.md) releases and packages. Native notifications use Fastframe on Linux, macOS and Windows. ZapFast keeps its account/chat routing, privacy settings, notification limits and sound previews. Clicks open the announced message; reading a chat withdraws its tracked notifications. OS permissions and notification presentation still apply. ## More native apps **Want Spotify just as fast and native?** [Spotifast](https://spotifast.rocks) is ZapFast's sibling. Both are built on [fastframe](https://fastframe.dev). ## Acknowledgements ZapFast uses [whatsapp-rust](https://github.com/oxidezap/whatsapp-rust), [egui](https://www.egui.rs), [fastframe](https://fastframe.dev), the [Inter](https://rsms.me/inter/) typeface and Noto Color Emoji (OFL), and [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) icons (ISC), also used for the chat wallpaper doodles. The notification sounds are [Pidgin](https://pidgin.im)'s, under the GPL-2.0 (see `assets/sounds/`). ZapFast is an unofficial client and is not affiliated with WhatsApp or Meta. Using an unofficial client may be against WhatsApp's terms of service and could get an account suspended. Use it at your own risk. WhatsApp is a trademark of WhatsApp LLC. Licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE). ## Star history
manifest_content:
[package]
name = "zapfast"
version = "0.21.1"
edition = "2024"
rust-version = "1.98"
license = "MIT"
description = "A native WhatsApp client built with Rust and egui"
homepage = "https://zapfast.rocks"
repository = "https://github.com/crmne/zapfast"
keywords = ["whatsapp", "chat", "egui", "messaging"]
categories = ["gui"]

[lib]
name = "zapfast"
path = "src/lib.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "zapfast"
path = "src/main.rs"

[dependencies]
anyhow = "1"
# Hashes saved stickers by content. Already included through wacore.
sha2 = "0.11"
# Already in the tree through rustls; verifies lock codes.
ring = "0.17"
# Decrypts Signal sticker packs. All four crates are already included through
# wacore at these versions.
aes = "0.9"
cbc = { version = "0.2", features = ["alloc", "block-padding"] }
hkdf = "0.13"
hmac = "0.13"
# Reads .wastickers and WhatsApp Lottie (.was) archives.
zip = { version = "9", default-features = false, features = ["deflate"] }
tempfile = "3"
# In-process Lottie rasterizer; no GIF encoder or native rendering dependency.
rasterlottie = { version = "0.2.4", default-features = false, features = ["images", "text"] }
clap = { version = "4.5", features = ["derive"] }
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"
log = "0.4"
directories = "6"
# UI framework. glow avoids the larger wgpu dependency.
eframe = { version = "0.36.2", default-features = false, features = ["accesskit", "glow", "default_fonts", "links", "wayland", "x11", "persistence"] }
egui = "0.36.2"
egui_extras = { version = "0.36.2", features = ["file", "image", "svg", "webp", "gif"] }
# Reads the colour emoji font's bitmaps for the demo tour's GIF fixtures. Keep
# skrifa aligned with epaint to avoid compiling two versions.
skrifa = "0.44"
# Decodes JPEG, PNG, WebP, and GIF images.
image = { version = "0.25", default-features = false, features = ["jpeg", "png", "webp", "gif"] }
# WhatsApp Web protocol: pairing, encryption, history sync, and media. Version
# 0.7.0 on crates.io enables `simd`, which needs nightly Rust. This commit builds
# on stable and includes snapshot recovery and no-progress conflict handling
# (upstream #1365, #1374 and #1375). Selected features provide Tokio transport,
# ureq media downloads, and the SQLite device store. The window handles shutdown
# instead of `signal`. Includes upstream Business pairing (#1440), LockChatUpdate
# and snapshot replay (#1507), the viewer's channel mute state (#1537), favorite
# and recent sticker sync events (#1538), boolean AB props (#1539), favorite
# chats sync (#1544), media re-upload that works and expired downloads that no
# longer force a media_conn refresh each (#1648, #1653, #1659; the 429s of
# ZapFast #405), and the typed send, edit, picture and poll APIs (#1614, #1626,
# #1630, #1640). Protobuf structs are non-exhaustive since #1676, so they are
# built from `Default` and assigned field by field. Device-store
# compatibility retains the legacy created_at column. All carried fixes have
# merged upstream, including video pacing, retransmission and loss recovery
# (#1726, #1727, #1728), the 1:1 report extension's bytes and rate received
# (#1761), without which an iPhone peer lowered its video to 600 kbit/s
# mid-call, and counters of why the peer's video packets never became pictures
# (#1763), which the call log prints. The sqlite-wasm-rs 0.6 edge that clashed
# with rusqlite 0.40 (#1764) is behind a `js` feature since #1765. This is
# upstream main with XOR FEC for 1:1 video, which an iPhone relies on since it
# never NACKs (#1783), dropping video queued before the relay allocates
# (#1782), interleaved video FEC against burst loss (#1789), video timed from
# capture so a peer can lip-sync it (#1790), and the native relay RTC stack on
# 0.21.1 (#1847). Back to crates.io once released. `voip` is the call stack:
# signaling, the sans-IO media engine with MLOW and libopus codecs, and the
# native UDP relay transport.
whatsapp-rust = { git = "https://github.com/oxidezap/whatsapp-rust", rev = "e634d245f71d66e2ae55f79ef714c4ca01615ed8", default-features = false, features = ["sqlite-storage", "tokio-transport", "tokio-runtime", "ureq-client", "tokio-native", "voip"] }
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "sync", "time", "macros", "fs", "net", "io-util"] }
# Queue between the call's audio streams and the engine.
async-channel = "2.5"
# Opens the WhatsApp WebSocket through a proxy. Both crates are already
# included through the Tokio transport at these versions.
tokio-websockets = { version = "0.13.3", default-features = false, features = ["client"] }
http = "1"
# Encodes HTTP proxy credentials. Already included through several crates.
base64 = "0.23"
# SQLCipher encrypts the archive; the device store shares the same library.
# Bundle OpenSSL so all release platforms use the same encryption provider.
rusqlite = { version = "0.40", features = ["bundled-sqlcipher-vendored-openssl"] }
keyring-core = "1"
getrandom = "0.4"
zeroize = "1"
rand = "0.10"

name: voxl
description: extremely fast web remote desktop streaming
readme_content:
# voxl

[![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/voxl-server.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/voxl-server)

Low-latency desktop streaming for the browser, written in Rust. voxl streams an X11
display, a Mac's screen or a Windows desktop as H.264 over a WebSocket to a small web
client that decodes with WebCodecs, with input, clipboard, audio, microphone, file and
folder transfer and dynamic resolution.

## Quick start

```sh
cargo install voxl-server   # needs x264, libyuv, Opus, PulseAudio and esbuild (see Usage)
DISPLAY=:1 voxl             # streams display :1 and prints a link that signs you in
```

Open the link it prints. On a Mac or a Windows PC, `voxl` streams that machine's own
screen instead; see [macOS](#macos) and [Windows](#windows).

## Benchmarks

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/acdf3f31-64fc-4acf-b5c5-ff173d7100a8

In every test below voxl averages 60 FPS with a median latency of 12–99 ms; noVNC
averages under 8 FPS.

A 16 vCPU AMD EPYC 9334 VM (no GPU), 2560x1600 Xvfb desktop, same workloads, each
stream decoded by a native client that reads a pixel marker drawn into the content.
Cells are FPS (worst second), then latency p50/p99 from the content being drawn to the
frame being decoded. voxl's column is its best run of each test. To reproduce, see
[`bench/`](bench/README.md).

| Test                           | voxl                       | [selkies](https://github.com/selkies-project/selkies) | [KasmVNC](https://github.com/kasmtech/KasmVNC) | [Neko](https://github.com/m1k1o/neko) | [Neko, tuned](https://github.com/m1k1o/neko) | [Sunshine](https://github.com/LizardByte/Sunshine) | [Sunshine, tuned](https://github.com/LizardByte/Sunshine) | [noVNC](https://github.com/novnc/noVNC) | [Daytona](https://www.daytona.io) |

- **selkies:** [selkies](https://github.com/selkies-project/selkies) with picom running.
- **KasmVNC:** 1.4.0 with a 60 FPS cap, JPEG/WebP quality 8–9 and video mode, no
  compositor.
- **Neko:** [m1k1o/neko](https://github.com/m1k1o/neko) 3.2 with its defaults (VP8, 25
  FPS). **Neko, tuned** captures at 60 FPS and encodes with x264 `ultrafast`/
  `zerolatency` at up to 30 Mbps, like voxl. Neither adapts its bitrate (Neko's
  estimator is off by default), so on slow links frames queue up; "stalls" means no
  frame arrived in 20 s.
- **Sunshine:** [Sunshine](https://github.com/LizardByte/Sunshine) 2025.628 streaming to
  Moonlight ([moonlight-embedded](https://github.com/moonlight-stream/moonlight-embedded)
  2.7, patched to hand frames to the benchmark client). Sunshine is built around GPU
  capture and encoding; without a GPU it falls back to copying the X11 screen and x264,
  so these numbers show it on a GPU-less VM like the other tests, not on the gaming PC
  it's made for. **Sunshine** runs its defaults (`superfast` on 2 threads) at Moonlight's
  default 40 Mbps; **Sunshine, tuned** uses `ultrafast` on 4 threads at 30 Mbps, like
  voxl (8 or 16 threads did no better). Neither reaches 60 FPS on this VM, and it keeps
  working while the screen is still (its idle CPU). Moonlight doesn't adapt its bitrate,
  so on slow links it's set to 80% of the link. Its CPU was measured in a later session,
  where voxl used 1.74, 1.65 and 1.99 cores on the same workloads.
- **noVNC:** x11vnc and noVNC as [E2B Desktop](https://github.com/e2b-dev/desktop)
  and Daytona ship them (`-forever -wait 50 -shared`, Tight encoding). x11vnc polls the
  screen, which caps it at 6–8 FPS.
- **Daytona:** a default sandbox (1 CPU, x11vnc and noVNC at 2560x1600) streamed
  through Daytona's signed preview proxy, about 12 ms away, which its latency includes.
  The workloads run inside the sandbox, sharing its CPU, and slow links are added on top
  of that internet path.
- **Links:** a bottleneck with a deep queue: a TCP proxy for the WebSocket servers, and
  `tc netem` for Neko's WebRTC media and Sunshine's video (UDP). None of them drop
  packets, where UDP with error correction would have the edge.

## Usage

Build (needs Rust, pkg-config, clang, x264, libyuv, libopus, libpulse and esbuild;
`nix-shell` provides them all):

```sh
nix-shell
cargo build --release
```

Or install it from [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/voxl-server) with the same
libraries on your system (the crate is `voxl-server`, the binary is `voxl`):

```sh
cargo install voxl-server
```

Run it against an X display, then open the link it prints (`?stats` adds an FPS
overlay):

```sh
DISPLAY=:1 ./target/release/voxl --port=6901
# prints: open http://localhost:6901/?token=4f1c… to sign in
```

Start Xvfb with `-shmem` for zero-copy capture, and use the patched Xvfb
(`nix-build -E 'with import <nixpkgs> {}; callPackage ./xvfb.nix {}'`) for smooth
scrolling. voxl accepts selkies' command-line flags; other selkies flags are ignored.
`voxl --help` lists every flag with its default, and `voxl --version` prints the version.

| Flag                                                           | Default                            |                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--addr`, `--port`                                             | `0.0.0.0`, `6901`                  | listen address                                                                                                    |
| `--title`                                                      | `Voxl Computer Stream`             | the page's title: the browser tab, and the app's name if a viewer installs it                                     |
| `--favicon`                                                    | voxl's icon                        | the tab's icon: an `.ico`, `.png`, `.gif`, `.webp` or `.svg` file                                                 |
| `--enable-basic-auth`                                          | `true`                             | ask for a password (see [Login](#login)); `false` serves without one                                              |
| `--basic-auth-password`                                        | `VOXL_PASSWORD`, else made up      | the password                                                                                                      |
| `--basic-auth-user`                                            | any                                | the user name a browser's sign-in has to give                                                                     |
| `--framerate`                                                  | `60`                               | max frames per second (`60-60` style ranges accepted)                                                             |
| `--preset`                                                     | `ultrafast`                        | x264 preset

name: gpui-kit
description: Rust GUI components for building fantastic cross-platform desktop application by using GPUI.
readme_content:
GPUI Kit

[English](./README.md) | [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md) [![Build Status](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-kit/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-kit/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Docs](https://docs.rs/gpui-kit/badge.svg)](https://docs.rs/gpui-kit/) [![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/gpui-kit.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/gpui-kit) Build fantastic, high-performance desktop apps with Rust and GPUI. GPUI Kit is a comprehensive Rust desktop application framework. It combines a production-ready UI system with application-grade data, layout, and editing capabilities, all built on a reusable foundation of behavior, state, and infrastructure. GPUI Kit ships 75+ documented components and primitives, WebAssembly support, AccessKit accessibility, UI integration testing, and an optional JavaScript extension runtime. Documentation: ```text gpui-kit The one crate applications depend on ├── gpui-base Unstyled behavior, state, and infrastructure └── gpui-component GPUI Component: the complete styled UI system ``` `gpui-kit` pins the matching GPUI release and re-exports GPUI, base, component, and assets, so a Rust application lists a single dependency. JavaScript extension hosts add `gpui-shell` separately; its default `components` feature supplies the styled catalog. See the [executable application recipe and AI-assisted development acceptance checks](examples/ai_recipes/README.md) for a tested starting point and verification commands. ## Features - **75+ Components and Primitives**: Forms, navigation, overlays, data display, editing, feedback, and layout, with polished interactions and productive defaults. - **Production Ready**: Used to build Longbridge Pro from day one and continuously refined in a publicly shipped commercial desktop application. - **WebAssembly**: Run applications and the same component showcases on the web with `wasm32-unknown-unknown`. - **Accessibility**: AccessKit roles, names, states, relationships, and actions are built into the interaction layer and covered by tests. - **UI Integration Testing**: Render real components in headless windows, drive pointer and keyboard input, and assert state, focus, layout, and accessibility. - **Native Feel**: Modern controls inspired by macOS and Windows, backed by semantic themes and multiple sizes. - **120 FPS**: GPU-accelerated interfaces that remain smooth under load. - **Data Tables**: Virtual scrolling, fixed and resizable columns, sorting, and cell selection across hundreds of thousands of rows. - **Virtual Lists**: Render only the visible range, including lists whose items have different sizes. - **Code Editor**: Stable performance at 200K lines with Tree-sitter highlighting and LSP diagnostics, completion, and hover. - **Dock Layout**: Resizable panels, draggable tabs, nested splits, and edge docks — all serializable. - **Rich Content**: Native Markdown and HTML rendering, syntax highlighting, and built-in charts. - **Design Freedom**: Use the complete visual system or build your own on the behavior and infrastructure in `gpui-base`. - **JavaScript Extensions**: `gpui-shell` lets a shipped Rust host load panels and business logic as scripts, with every capability granted explicitly. - **Cross Platform**: Ship one Rust codebase to macOS, Windows, and Linux. ## Framework Architecture ### Three layers. One ecosystem. Use `gpui-component` to keep the application coherent with one complete visual and interaction system. Use `gpui-base` when your product needs to create and own that system itself. Use `gpui-shell` when the application should be extensible in JavaScript after it ships. | **`gpui-component`** | **`gpui-base`** | **`gpui-shell`** | | -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | | Complete, styled components | Unstyled behavior and infrastructure | JavaScript runtime hosted by Rust | | Productive defaults with theming | Full control over structure and visual design | Capabilities granted one at a time | | Best for building applications | Best for building design systems | Best for plugins and scripted applications | ```text APPLICATION │ ┌───────────────────┼───────────────────┐ │ │ │ ▼ ▼ ▼ ┌──────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────┐ │ gpui-component │ │ Your Design │ │ gpui-shell │ │ Styled UI │ │ System │ │ JS extensions │ └────────┬─────────┘ └────────┬─────────┘ └────────┬─────────┘ │ │ │ └────────────────────┼────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌──────────────────┐ │ gpui-base │ │ Behavior · State │ │ Infrastructure │ └────────┬─────────┘ ▼ GPUI ``` > **Behavior belongs to the foundation. Presentation belongs to the application.** Use **`gpui-component`** when you want polished controls ready to ship. Build on **`gpui-base`** when your application should own its component source, layout, styling, and motion while reusing difficult interaction behavior. Add **`gpui-shell`** when contributors should extend the product without a fork or a release. The layering follows the same separation that makes the [shadcn](https://ui.shadcn.com) ecosystem flexible: | GPUI Kit ecosystem | Web ecosystem | | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------- | | GPUI | HTML + Tailwind CSS | | [`gpui-base`](crates/base/README.md) | [Base UI](https://base-ui.com) | | `gpui-component` | shadcn's styled component layer | [Explore the architecture →](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) ## Showcase GPUI Kit has powered [Longbridge Pro](https://longbridge.com/desktop) from day one. The framework is extracted from the demands of a publicly shipped commercial desktop application rather than designed in isolation. > **GPUI provides the rendering foundation. Longbridge provides the production foundation.** ## Usage ```toml [dependencies] gpui-kit = "0.7" ``` `gpui-kit` always brings in GPUI and `gpui-base`; `gpui-component` and the default icon set are on by default. Turn default features off to keep only the layers you use. The `gpui-component` features (`inspector`, `decimal`, `tree-sitter`, and each `tree-sitter-`) are available under the same names. ### GPUI Fast Enable the optional `gpui-fast` feature to select [GPUI Fast](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-fast) for the core, native platforms, WebAssembly, and every enabled Kit layer: ```toml [dependencies] gpui-kit = { version = "0.7", features = ["gpui-fast"] } ``` Keep the same imports, initialization, and test macros; no application `[patch]` or crate alias is needed. The default backend remains the pinned upstream GPUI snapshot. Cargo features are additive, so upstream packages still compile when Fast is selected. See [Getting Started](https://gpui-kit.com/docs/getting-started) for feature combinations and comparison commands. ### Basic Example ```rs use gpui_kit::component::button::*; use gpui_kit::component::*; use gpui_kit::*; pub struct HelloWorld; impl Render for HelloWorld { fn render(&mut self, _: &mut Window, _: &mut Context) -> impl IntoElement { div() .v_flex() .gap_2() .size_full() .items_center() .justify_center() .child("Hello, World!") .child( Button::new("ok") .primary() .label("Let's Go!") .on_click(|_, _, _| println!("Clicked!")), ) } } fn main() { gpui_kit::application().run(move |cx| { // This must be called before using any GPUI Component features. gpui_kit::init(cx); gpui_kit::open_window(WindowOptions::default(), cx, |_, cx| { cx.new(|_| HelloWorld) }) .expect("Failed to open window"); }); } ``` `gpui_kit::open_window` is the application window entry point and always mounts a Base `Root`. Component initialization registers styled window facilities; Cargo features do not select a different root type. ### Icons The default `assets` feature bundles the [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) icon set as `gpui-kit-assets`; pass it to the application with `gpui_kit::application().with_assets(gpui_kit::assets::Assets)`. To ship your own icons instead, leave that feature out and name the SVG files as defined in [IconName](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-kit/blob/main/crates/component/src/icon.rs#L86). ## Skills for AI Coding Agents Install the GPUI Kit skills for your AI coding agent (Cursor, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, etc.): ```bash npx skills add longbridge/gpui-kit ``` | Skill | Description | | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `gpui-kit` | Setup, component catalog, usage patterns, GPUI mechanics (elements, entities, async, focus, actions, tests), and the Coding Guides. | | `gpui-kit-design-guides` | The Design Guides: layout, spacing, hierarchy, interaction states, overlays, and interface copy. | ## Development ### Desktop Gallery (Story) The `story` crate is a gallery application that showcases all available components. Run it with: ```bash cargo run ``` ### Examples Some larger examples reuse the `story` gallery components and run as standalone packages: ```bash # Dock layout system (panels, split views, tabs) cargo run -p example-dock # Markdown rendering cargo run -p example-markdown # HTML rendering cargo run -p example-html ``` The `examples` directory also contains standalone examples, each focused on a single feature. Each example is a separate crate, run them with `cargo run -p `: ```bash # Code editor with LSP support and syntax highlighting cargo run -p example-editor # Basic hello world cargo run -p hello_world # System monitor (real-time charts with CPU/memory data) cargo run -p system_monitor # Window title customization cargo run -p window_title ``` Check out [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for more details. ## Compare to others See the [comparison with Iced, egui and Qt 6](https://gpui-kit.com/docs/comparison) on the site. ## Related project: Native Shell [Native Shell](https://nsh.dev) ([source](https://github.com/longbridge/native-shell)) is a sibling project that lets AI generate UI and renders it natively on iOS, Android, Linux (GTK) and macOS (AppKit). Its GPUI desktop backend is in development and will be built on GPUI Kit. ## License Software source and documentation code examples: [Apache-2.0](LICENSE-APACHE). Documentation prose and original illustrations in the Docs, Base, Component, and Shell sections (including Chinese translations) for which GPUI Kit holds licensing rights are also o

# crates carry to crates.io, so they pin the exact snapshot the release was
# built against: a caret requirement let the weekly release move applications
# onto a newer snapshot that gpui-component did not compile with (#3156). Bump
# every snapshot crate together with its Cargo.lock entry; `script/check-gpui-pin.ts`
# fails CI when a pin is not exact.
gpui = { package = "gpui-pre", version = "=0.3.11" }
gpui_platform = { package = "gpui-pre-platform", version = "=0.3.11", features = ["font-kit", "x11", "wayland", "runtime_shaders"] }
gpui_web = { package = "gpui-pre-web", version = "=0.3.11" }
# Fast is optional; existing crates select it through their gpui-fast feature.
# Explicit package fields make Cargo use these dependency keys as Rust crate names;
# the packages declare the same library names as the pre backend.
gpui-fast = { package = "gpui-fast", version = "0.1.13", features = ["windows-manifest-provided-by-host"] }
gpui-fast-platform = { package = "gpui-fast-platform", version = "0.1.13", features = ["font-kit", "x11", "wayland", "runtime_shaders"] }
gpui-fast-web = { package = "gpui-fast-web", version = "0.1.13" }
gpui_macros = { package = "gpui-pre-macros", version = "=0.3.11" }
reqwest_client = { package = "gpui-pre-reqwest-client", version = "=0.3.11" }
sum-tree = { package = "gpui-pre-sum-tree", version = "=0.3.11" }
reqwest = { package = "gpui-pre-reqwest", version = "=0.12.15", default-features = false, features = [
    "charset",
    "http2",
    "macos-system-configuration",
    "multipart",
    "rustls-tls-native-roots",
    "socks",
    "stream",
] }

anyhow = "1"
instant = { version = "0.1", features = ["wasm-bindgen"] }
log = "0.4"
lsp-types = { version = "0.97.0", features = ["proposed"] }
notify = "8.2.0"
raw-window-handle = "0.6.2"
ropey = { version = "=2.0.0-beta.1", features = [
    "metric_chars",
    "metric_lines_lf",
    "metric_utf16",
] }
rust-i18n = "4.2.0"
schemars = "1"
semver = "1"
serde = { version = "1.0.219", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"
serde_repr = "0.1"
smallvec = "1"
smol = "2"

    "parsing",

    "regex-fancy",
] }
two-face = { version = "0.4.5", default-features = false, features = ["syntect-fancy"] }
tracing = "0.1.41"
wasm-bindgen = "0.2.113"
# Use errno stub for WASM
errno = { version = "0.3.14", default-features = false }

[workspace.dependencies.windows]
features = ["Wdk", "Wdk_System", "Wdk_System_SystemServices"]
version = "0.58.0"

[workspace.lints.clippy]
almost_complete_range = "allow"
arc_with_non_send_sync = "allow"
borrowed_box = "allow"
dbg_macro = "deny"
let_underscore_future = "allow"

name: ai-goofish-monitor
description: 基于 Playwright 和AI实现的闲鱼多任务实时/定时监控与智能分析系统，配备了功能完善的后台管理UI。帮助用户从闲鱼海量商品中，找到心仪产品。
readme_content:
# 闲鱼智能监控系统

[中文] ｜ [English](README_EN.md)

基于 Playwright 和 AI 的闲鱼多任务实时监控，提供完整的 Web 管理界面。


## 核心特性

- **Web 可视化管理**: 任务管理、账号管理、AI 标准编辑、运行日志、结果浏览
- **AI 驱动**: 自然语言创建任务，多模态模型深度分析商品
- **多任务并发**: 独立配置关键词、价格、筛选条件和 AI Prompt
- **高级筛选**: 包邮、新发布时间范围、省/市/区三级区域筛选
- **即时通知**: 支持 ntfy.sh、企业微信、Bark、Telegram、Webhook等多渠道
- **定时调度**: 支持 Cron 配置周期性任务
- **账号与代理轮换**: 多账号管理、任务绑定账号、代理池轮换与失败重试
- **Docker 部署**: 一键容器化部署

## 截图

![监控概览](static/img.png)
![任务管理](static/img_1.png)
![结果查看](static/img_2.png)
![通知推送](static/img_3.png)

## 🐳 Docker 部署（推荐）

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Usagi-org/ai-goofish-monitor && cd ai-goofish-monitor
cp .env.example .env
vim .env # 填写相关配置项
docker compose up -d
docker compose logs -f app
docker compose down
```

如果镜像无法访问或下载速度慢，可尝试使用加速：
```bash

docker pull ghcr.nju.edu.cn/usagi-org/ai-goofish:latest
docker tag ghcr.nju.edu.cn/usagi-org/ai-goofish:latest ghcr.io/usagi-org/ai-goofish:latest
docker compose up -d

```

- 默认 Web UI 地址：`http://127.0.0.1:8000`
- Docker 镜像已内置 Chromium，无需宿主机额外安装浏览器。
- 官方镜像地址：`ghcr.io/usagi-org/ai-goofish:latest`
- 更新镜像：`docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`
- 如果你修改了 `.env` 中的 `SERVER_PORT`，请同步更新 `docker-compose.yaml` 里的端口映射。
- `docker-compose.yaml` 默认会把 SQLite 主库挂载到 `./data:/app/data`，数据库文件默认为 `data/app.sqlite3`
- 目前默认持久化这些目录：
    - `data/`  SQLite 主存储（任务、结果、价格历史）
    - `state/`  登录状态 cookie 文件
    - `prompts/`  任务提示词
    - `logs/`  运行日志
    - `images/`  商品图片与任务临时图片目录
    - `config.json`、`jsonl/`、`price_history/`  首次升级到 SQLite 时用于兼容导入的旧数据源

### 数据存储与迁移

- 当前在线主存储为 SQLite，默认路径 `data/app.sqlite3`
- 可通过环境变量 `APP_DATABASE_FILE` 自定义数据库路径；Docker 默认设置为 `/app/data/app.sqlite3`
- 应用启动时会自动建库建表，并尝试从旧的 `config.json`、`jsonl/`、`price_history/` 导入一次历史数据
- `state/`、`prompts/`、`logs/`、`images/` 仍然是文件系统目录，不在 SQLite 中
- 商品图片会临时落到 `images/task_images_<task_name>/`，任务结束后默认会清理
- 首次升级完成并确认 `data/app.sqlite3` 中数据正确后，可视部署方式决定是否继续保留旧的 `config.json`、`jsonl/`、`price_history/` 挂载

### 最少配置

| 变量 | 说明 | 必填 |
|------|------|------|
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | AI 模型 API Key | 是 |
| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | OpenAI 兼容接口地址 | 是 |
| `OPENAI_MODEL_NAME` | 支持图片输入的模型名称 | 是 |
| `WEB_USERNAME` / `WEB_PASSWORD` | Web UI 登录账号密码，默认 `admin/admin123` | 否 |

其余配置见下方“配置说明”。


### 第一次使用

1. 打开默认 Web UI `http://127.0.0.1:8000` 并登录。
2. 进入“闲鱼账号管理”，使用 [Chrome 扩展](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/xianyu-login-state-extrac/eidlpfjiodpigmfcahkmlenhppfklcoa) 导出并粘贴闲鱼登录态 JSON。
3. 登录态文件会保存到 `state/` 目录，例如 `state/acc_1.json`。
4. 回到“任务管理”，创建任务并绑定账号后即可运行。

### 创建第一个任务

- `AI判断`：填写“详细需求”，提交后会弹出独立进度弹窗，后台异步生成分析标准。
- `关键词判断`：填写关键词规则，任务会直接创建，不经过 AI 生成流程。
- `区域筛选`：已改为省 / 市 / 区三级选择器，数据基于闲鱼页面抓取快照内置。



## 用户使用说明

<details>
<summary>点击展开 Web UI 功能说明</summary>

### 任务管理

- 支持 AI 创建、关键词规则、价格范围、新发布范围、区域筛选、账号绑定、定时规则。
- AI 任务创建是后台 job 流程，提交后会打开单独的进度弹窗。
- 区域筛选会显著缩小结果集，默认留空。

### 账号管理

- 支持导入、更新、删除闲鱼账号登录态。
- 每个任务可指定账号，也可不绑定并交给系统自动选择。

### 结果查看与运行日志

- 结果页和导出功能现在从 SQLite 查询，不再直接扫描 `jsonl` 文件。
- 日志页按任务展示运行过程，便于排查登录态失效、风控和 AI 调用问题。

### 系统设置

- 可查看系统状态、编辑 Prompt、调整代理与轮换相关配置。

</details>



## 开发者开发

### 环境要求

- Python 3.10+
- Node.js + npm（本地验证 `Node v20.18.3` 可完成前端构建）
- Playwright CLI 与 Chromium，首次运行前建议执行 `python3 -m pip install playwright && python3 -m playwright install chromium`
- Chrome / Edge 浏览器（Linux 环境也可使用 Chromium；`start.sh` 会先检查浏览器是否存在）

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Usagi-org/ai-goofish-monitor
cd ai-goofish-monitor
cp .env.example .env
```

### 一键启动

```bash
chmod +x start.sh
./start.sh
```

`start.sh` 会先检查 Playwright CLI 和浏览器前置条件；在前置条件满足后自动安装项目依赖、构建前端、复制构建产物并启动后端。

### 手动启动

```bash
# 后端
python -m src.app
# 或
uvicorn src.app:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --reload

# 前端
cd web-ui
npm install
npm run dev
```

- FastAPI 启动时会自动初始化 SQLite，并在首次启动时尝试导入旧的 `config.json/jsonl/price_history`
- `spider_v2.py` 默认从 SQLite 读取任务；只有显式传入 `--config <path>` 时才会走 JSON 配置兼容模式
- 默认数据库路径为 `data/app.sqlite3`
- Vite 开发服务器会将 `/api`、`/auth`、`/ws` 代理到 `http://127.0.0.1:8000`。
- `npm run build` 先生成 `web-ui/dist/`，`start.sh` 再复制到仓库根目录 `dist/`。
- FastAPI 负责提供根目录 `dist/index.html` 和 `dist/assets/`。
- `./start.sh` 默认输出访问地址 `http://localhost:8000` 和 API 文档 `http://localhost:8000/docs`。

### 测试与校验

```bash
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 pytest
cd web-ui && npm run build
```

### 任务创建 API

<details>
<summary>点击展开 API 行为说明</summary>

- `POST /api/tasks/generate`
  - `decision_mode=ai`：返回 `202` 和 `job`，需要继续轮询进度。
  - `decision_mode=keyword`：直接返回已创建任务。
- `GET /api/tasks/generate-jobs/{job_id}`：查询 AI 任务生成进度。
- `POST /auth/status`：校验 Web UI 登录凭据。

</details>

## 配置说明

<details>
<summary>点击展开常用配置项</summary>

### AI 与运行时

- `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_BASE_URL` / `OPENAI_MODEL_NAME`：AI 模型接入必填项。
- `PROXY_URL`：为 AI 请求单独指定 HTTP/SOCKS5 代理。
- `RUN_HEADLESS`：是否以无头模式运行爬虫；Docker 中应保持 `true`。
- `SERVER_PORT`：后端监听端口，默认 `8000`。
- `LOGIN_IS_EDGE`：本地环境可切换为 Edge 内核；Docker 镜像未内置 Edge，容器内会固定使用 Chromium。
- `PCURL_TO_MOBILE`：是否将 PC 商品链接转换为移动端链接。

### 通知

- `NTFY_TOPIC_URL`
- `GOTIFY_URL` / `GOTIFY_TOKEN`
- `BARK_URL`
- `WX_BOT_URL`
- `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` / `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` / `TELEGRAM_API_BASE_URL`
- `WEBHOOK_*`

### 代理轮换与失败保护

- `PROXY_ROTATION_ENABLED`
- `PROXY_ROTATION_MODE`
- `PROXY_POOL`
- `PROXY_ROTATION_RETRY_LIMIT`
- `PROXY_BLACKLIST_TTL`
- `TASK_FAILURE_THRESHOLD`
- `TASK_FAILURE_PAUSE_SECONDS`
- `TASK_FAILURE_GUARD_PATH`

完整示例见 `.env.example`。

</details>

## Web 界面认证

<details>
<summary>点击展开认证说明</summary>

- Web UI 当前使用登录页收集账号密码，并通过 `POST /auth/status` 校验。
- 登录成功后，前端会在浏览器本地保存登录状态，用于路由守卫和 WebSocket 初始化。
- 默认账号密码为 `admin/admin123`，生产环境请务必修改。

</details>

## 🚀 工作流程

下图描述了单个监控任务从启动到完成的核心处理逻辑。主服务运行于 `src.app`，按用户操作或定时调度启动一个或多个任务进程。

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[启动监控任务] --> B[选择账号/代理配置];
    B --> C[任务: 搜索商品];
    C --> D{发现新商品?};
    D -- 是 --> E[抓取商品详情 & 卖家信息];
    E --> F[下载商品图片];
    F --> G[调用AI进行分析];
    G --> H{AI是否推荐?};
    H -- 是 --> I[发送通知];
    H -- 否 --> J[保存记录到 SQLite];
    I --> J;
    D -- 否 --> K[翻页/等待];
    K --> C;
    J --> C;
    C --> L{触发风控/异常?};
    L -- 是 --> M[账号/代理轮换并重试];
    M --> C;
```

## 常见问题

<details>
<summary>点击展开常见问题</summary>

### AI 任务创建为什么不是立即完成？

AI 模式会先生成分析标准，再创建任务。现在该流程已改为后台 job，提交后会显示独立进度弹窗，避免表单长时间卡住。

### 区域筛选为什么默认建议留空？

区域筛选会显著减少搜索结果，适合明确只看某个区域的场景。若你先验证整体市场，建议先不填。

### 本地页面打开后提示前端构建产物不存在？

说明根目录 `dist/` 缺失。可直接执行 `./start.sh`，或先在 `web-ui/` 里执行 `npm run build`，再确认构建产物已复制到仓库根目录。

### `./start.sh` 为什么提示缺少 Playwright 或浏览器？

这是脚本的前置检查。请先安装 Playwright CLI 与 Chromium，并确保系统中可用 Chrome / Edge（Linux 环境也可用 Chromium），然后重新执行 `./start.sh`。

</details>

name: figma-console-mcp
description: Your design system as an API. Connect AI to Figma for extraction, creation, and debugging.
readme_content:
# Figma Console MCP Server

[![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-Compatible-blue)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/)
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/figma-console-mcp)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/figma-console-mcp)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
[![Documentation](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-docs.figma--console--mcp.southleft.com-0D9488)](https://docs.figma-console-mcp.southleft.com)
[![Sponsor](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sponsor-southleft-ea4aaa?logo=github-sponsors&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/sponsors/southleft)

> **Your design system as an API.** A design-system-focused Model Context Protocol server for Figma. It works in both directions (Figma ⇄ code), **writes to Figma**, and runs **deterministic checks** for design-code parity, accessibility, and design-system health. It hands the AI exact tokens, variants, bindings, and states as structured data rather than prescribing a framework or house style, so generated code follows your team's own stack and conventions.

> **🆕 Shaders, grid and auto layout, OKLCH and P3 color, text wrap and variable fonts (latest v1.46.0):** apply shaders and set their properties by name (`figma_apply_shader`, `figma_list_shaders`), set auto layout or grid layout in one call with CSS-style grid tracks (`figma_set_layout`), use OKLCH, Display P3 and other CSS colors on fills and strokes, and set text wrap (balance, pretty) and variable-font axes with `figma_set_text` (v1.46.0). v1.45 added Motion: animate layers with presets, custom animation styles or keyframes bound to Timing and Easing tokens, export video, and find code layers. [See what's new →](CHANGELOG.md#1460---2026-10-29)

## What is this?

Figma Console MCP connects AI assistants (like Claude) to Figma, enabling:

- **🎨 Design system extraction** - Pull variables, components, and styles
- **🧬 Codebase → design system extraction** - Scan a production codebase, mine its de-facto styling into DTCG tokens with per-token provenance, scaffold a design-system package with a wired Storybook workshop, and gate it with deterministic fidelity evals — then round-trip the tokens into Figma variables (Local Mode)
- **🔁 Bidirectional token sync** - Export Figma variables to DTCG JSON (legacy or 2025.10 dialect) + 9 more formats; push code-side edits back to Figma with full apply — creates, renames, alias re-targeting, and replace-gated deletes. Replaces Style Dictionary and Tokens Studio's export pipeline.
- **📸 Visual debugging** - Take screenshots for context
- **✏️ Design creation** - Create UI components, frames, and layouts directly in Figma — including one-call component-set creation from a variant axes matrix
- **🔧 Variable management** - Create, update, rename, and delete design tokens
- **🕰 Version history & time-series awareness** - List versions, diff snapshots, generate markdown changelogs, trace property/variant introduction via binary-search blame, and fold per-component design + git history into generated component docs
- **⚡ Real-time monitoring** - Watch console logs from the Desktop Bridge plugin
- **📌 FigJam boards** - Create stickies, flowcharts, tables, and code blocks on collaborative boards
- **🎞️ Slides presentations** - Build and manage Figma Slides decks programmatically
- **♿ Accessibility scanning** - 14 WCAG design checks with conformance level tagging, component scorecards, axe-core code scanning, design-to-code parity
- **🔍 Design-code parity & component docs** - Deterministic comparison of a Figma component with its code (visual, spacing, typography, tokens, component API, accessibility), and generated component documentation with per-variant tokens and an optional design + git changelog
- **📋 Design-system health audits** - Lighthouse-style scored audit across naming, tokens, component metadata, accessibility, consistency, and coverage — available as a plain tool for any MCP client (with per-finding auto-fix guidance) and as a visual dashboard app
- **🛡 Cross-MCP identity** - Every tool response carries `_mcp: "figma-console-mcp"` and errors are prefixed `[figma-console-mcp]` so attribution stays unambiguous in agents running multiple Figma MCPs
- **☁️ Cloud Write Relay** - Web AI clients (Claude.ai, v0, Replit) can design in Figma via cloud pairing
- **🔄 Four ways to connect** - Remote SSE, Cloud Mode, NPX, or Local Git

---

## ⚡ Quick Start

### Choose Your Setup

**First, decide what you want to do:**

| I want to... | Setup Method | Time |
|--------------|--------------|------|
| **Create and modify designs with AI** | [NPX Setup](#-npx-setup-recommended) (Recommended) | ~10 min |
| **Design from the web** (Claude.ai, v0, Replit, Lovable) | [Cloud Mode](#-cloud-mode-web-ai-clients) | ~5 min |
| **Contribute to the project** | [Local Git Setup](#for-contributors-local-git-mode) | ~15 min |
| **Just explore my design data** (read-only) | [Remote SSE](#-remote-sse-read-only-exploration) | ~2 min |

### ⚠️ Important: Capability Differences

| Capability | NPX / Local Git | Cloud Mode | Remote SSE |
|------------|-----------------|------------|------------|
| Read design data | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| **Create components & frames** | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
| **Edit existing designs** | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
| **Manage design tokens/variables** | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
| **FigJam boards (stickies, flowcharts)** | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
| Real-time monitoring (console, selection) | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| Codebase → design system extraction (`figma_ds_*`) | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| Desktop Bridge plugin | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
| Requires Node.js | Yes | **No** | No |
| **Total tools available** | **130** | **105** after pairing | Read-only subset |

> **Bottom line:** Remote SSE is **read-only** until you pair the plugin. **Cloud Mode** unlocks write access (105 tools) from web AI clients without Node.js. NPX/Local Git gives the full 130 tools with real-time monitoring.

---

### 🚀 NPX Setup (Recommended)

**Best for:** Designers who want full AI-assisted design capabilities.

**What you get:** All 130 tools including design creation, variable management, and component instantiation.

#### Prerequisites

- [ ] **Node.js 18+** — Check with `node --version` ([Download](https://nodejs.org))
- [ ] **Figma Desktop** installed (not just the web app)
- [ ] **An MCP client** (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Desktop, etc.)

#### Step 1: Get Your Figma Token

1. Go to [Manage personal access tokens](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/8085703771159-Manage-personal-access-tokens) in Figma Help
2. Follow the steps to **create a new personal access token**
3. Enter description: `Figma Console MCP`
4. Set scopes (all Read unless noted): **File content**, **File versions**, **Library content**, **Library assets**, **Comments** (Read and write), **Current user**, and **Variables** (Enterprise only, optional). See [why each is needed](https://docs.figma-console-mcp.southleft.com/setup#step-1-get-your-figma-token-2-min)
5. **Copy the token** — you won't see it again! (starts with `figd_`)

#### Step 2: Configure Your MCP Client

**Claude Code (CLI):**
```bash
claude mcp add figma-console -s user -e FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN=figd_YOUR_TOKEN_HERE -e ENABLE_MCP_APPS=true -- npx -y figma-console-mcp@latest
```

**OpenAI Codex (CLI):**
```bash
codex mcp add figma-console --env FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN=figd_YOUR_TOKEN_HERE --env ENABLE_MCP_APPS=true -- npx -y figma-console-mcp@latest
```
Then set `startup_timeout_sec = 60` and `tool_timeout_sec = 300` for it in `~/.codex/config.toml` (Codex's 10 s / 60 s defaults are too short). The Codex app and IDE extension share this config. [Full Codex setup →](https://docs.figma-console-mcp.southleft.com/setup#-openai-codex)

**Gemini CLI:**
```bash
gemini mcp add -s user -e FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN=figd_YOUR_TOKEN_HERE -e ENABLE_MCP_APPS=true figma-console npx -y figma-console-mcp@latest
```

**Google Antigravity (IDE, CLI, app):** add the JSON below to `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json`, plus `"timeoutSeconds": 300` in the server entry. [Full Antigravity setup →](https://docs.figma-console-mcp.southleft.com/setup#-google-antigravity)

**Cursor / Windsurf / Claude Desktop:**

Add to your MCP config file (see [Where to find your config file](#-where-to-find-your-config-file) below):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "figma-console": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "figma-console-mcp@latest"],
      "env": {
        "FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN": "figd_YOUR_TOKEN_HERE",
        "ENABLE_MCP_APPS": "true"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

#### 📂 Where to Find Your Config File

If you're not sure where to put the JSON configuration above, here's where each app stores its MCP config:

| App | macOS | Windows |
|-----|-------|---------|
| **Claude Desktop** | `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` | `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` |
| **Claude Code (CLI)** | `~/.claude.json` | `%USERPROFILE%\.claude.json` |
| **Cursor** | `~/.cursor/mcp.json` | `%USERPROFILE%\.cursor\mcp.json` |
| **Windsurf** | `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json` | `%USERPROFILE%\.codeium\windsurf\mcp_config.json` |
| **OpenAI Codex** (app, CLI, IDE) | `~/.codex/config.toml` (TOML, [see format](https://docs.figma-console-mcp.southleft.com/setup#-openai-codex)) | `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\config.toml` |
| **Gemini CLI** | `~/.gemini/settings.json` | `%USERPROFILE%\.gemini\settings.json` |
| **Google Antigravity** (IDE, CLI, app) | `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json` | `%USERPROFILE%\.gemini\config\mcp_config.json` |

> **Tip for designers:** The `~` symbol means your **home folder**. On macOS, that's `/Users/YourName/`. On Windows, it's `C:\Users\YourName\`. You can open these files in any text editor — even TextEdit or Notepad.
>
> **Can't find the file?** If it doesn't exist yet, create it. The app will pick it up on its next restart. Make sure the entire file is valid JSON (watch for missing commas or brackets).
>
> **Claude Code users:** You can skip manual editing entirely. Just run the `claude mcp add` command above and it handles everything for you.

#### Step 3: Connect to Figma Desktop

**Desktop Bridge Plugin:**
1. Open Figma Desktop normally (no special flags needed) and open a file
2. Go to **Plugins → Development → Import plugin from manifest...**
3. Select `~/.figma-console-mcp/plugin/manifest.json` (stable path, auto-created by the MCP server). Run `npx figma-console-mcp --print-path` to print the exact path for your machine.
4. Run the plugin in your Figma file — it scans ports 9223–9232 and connects automatically to your running MCP server

> **Can't see the folder in the import dialog?** `.figma-console-mcp` starts with a dot, so macOS hides it. In the dialog, press **⌘⇧G** and paste the path (or press **⌘⇧.** to show hidden files). On Windows the folder is visible as normal.

> **Heads-up on plugin updates.** Figma caches plugin files (`code.js` and `ui.html`) at the application level. The MCP server refreshes the files at `~/.figma-console-mcp/plugin/` on every startup, but Figma keeps using its cached copy until you re-import the manifest.
>
> **Re-importing is _required_ only when a release notes entry says so** — typically when the plugin adds a new method the server needs (e.g. v1.22.4, v1.10.0). The plugin files last changed in v1.41.5; if your imported plugin predates that, re-import once. The plugin shows an update banner when the server bundles a newer plugin than the one running. For most upgrades the new server stays wire-compatible with the previous plugin, and re-importing is **optional**: you'll still get every functional change, just not the cosmetic plugin-side touches (status-pill copy, `pluginVersion` reporting).
>
> When you do re-import: Plugins → Manage plugins → re-import `~/.figma-console-mcp/plugin/manifest.json`. The stable path never changes, so it's a one-click step.

#### Step 4: Restart Your MCP Client

Restart your MCP client to load the new configuration.

#### Step 5: Test It!

```
Check Fi

[License](#license) | --- ### [`motion-showreel`](./skills/motion-showreel) ![Motion Showreel Skill](./dist/imgs/covers/motion-showreel.webp) **Category:** Motion Graphics / Code Video **Best for:** showreels, product films, UI motion, kinetic typography, logo/title sequences, generative loops, retrospectives and narrated explainers. Short pieces typically run 5–60 s; chapter-based films support up to 20 minutes. `motion-showreel` delivers MP4 plus editable source. It confirms the topic, duration, orientation, independent music/SFX sources and narration mode, then writes a brief and confirms style frames. Deterministic `render(t)` pages are captured frame by frame on a shared audio/picture timeline. Narration follows a user-supplied script or recording; pictures follow actual speech timings. Long films use persistent chapter caches and technical acceptance. Highlights: - **Deterministic `render(t)` pipeline**: stills, contact sheets, three-direction boards, proxies and masters all come from the same page. Motion blur, supersampling and film grain are render flags. - **One timeline for picture and sound**: cuts, hits and SFX share the same numbers. Music can be synthesized (a zero-dependency built-in synth, or Tone.js with a sampled piano), or cut to the user's own track with beat and drop detection. - **A 43-style library as a starting point**: swiss-editorial, ink-wash, risograph, synthwave, soft 3D, cinematic title, pixel game, comic panels, guochao patterns, painterly strokes, whiteboard explainers, concept morphs, illuminated manuscripts and more. Each style defines its look, motion, camera grammar and sound palette, and can be adapted, mixed or replaced with your own. - **A sound direction, not a default song**: the brief sets a sound benchmark, groove, harmony, palette and dramatic arc, plus a list of audio defaults to avoid. - **Two checkpoints**: confirm requirements, then style frames (three distinct directions when unspecified), followed by autonomous production. Creative freedom remains available. - **Narration and long films**: Gemini/MiniMax TTS reads only user-supplied scripts; recordings use real timestamps. Music and SFX have independent sources, yield to speech, and chapter builds support up to 20 minutes. - **Technical acceptance kept separate from taste**: size, fps, duration, frame count, black frames, loudness, true peak, loop seam and determinism must all PASS. Review notes go to the user, who makes the final call.

name: e2e
description: Next generation e2e testing framework for web and mobile apps.
readme_content: # e2e [e2e](https://e2e.com?utm_source=e2e&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=readme_intro) is an end-to-end testing framework for web and mobile apps. Describe a goal in natural language and an agent drives the app to reach it. Check the result with locators and assertions in the same test. ```ts // tests/checkout.e2e.ts import { test, expect } from 'e2e'; test('a member upgrades to Pro', async ({ app, agent, screen }) => { await app.open('/settings/billing'); await agent.act('upgrade the workspace to the Pro plan'); await agent.assert('the invoice preview shows a prorated amount'); await expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toContainText('Pro'); }); ``` An agent step that a later assertion verifies records its actions, and the next run replays them with no model calls until the app changes. Tests without agent steps need no model. Bring your own subscription, API key, or local model. ## Quick start ```bash npx e2e init ``` `init` asks for an engine, web or mobile, and a model provider, then writes a config and an example test. The [quickstart](https://e2e.com/docs/quickstart) covers the rest. To see a finished setup in your stack, open [`examples/`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/tree/main/examples): Vite, Next.js, Astro, Angular, Expo, SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose, Kotlin Multiplatform, Flutter, and .NET MAUI, each a standalone project with a passing suite. ## Packages ### Core | Package | What it does | | --- | --- | | [`e2e`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/e2e) | The SDK, runner, and CLI. | | [`@e2e-dev/web`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@e2e-dev/web) | Browser engine: Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit through Playwright. | | [`@e2e-dev/mobile`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@e2e-dev/mobile) | iOS and Android engine: simulators and emulators through agent-device. | | [`@e2e-dev/decision`](https://e2e.com/docs/decision-models) | Decision-model executors for bounded semantic actions and assertions, and `decisionFilter()`, which leaves out the tests a pull request is unlikely to affect. | | [`@e2e-dev/acp`](https://e2e.com/docs/subscriptions#use-your-coding-agent) | Runs agent steps on your own coding agent (Claude Code or Codex) over the Agent Client Protocol. | ### Integrations | Package | What it does | | --- | --- | | [`@e2e-dev/kernel`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@e2e-dev/kernel) | Kernel hosted browsers for the web engine. | | [`@e2e-dev/lightpanda`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@e2e-dev/lightpanda) | Lightpanda, the open-source headless browser, started per run for the web engine. | | [`@e2e-dev/smol`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@e2e-dev/smol) | smol machines browsers for the web engine: by default, each attempt branches a warm Chromium microVM. | | [`@e2e-dev/testmu`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@e2e-dev/testmu) | TestMu AI (formerly LambdaTest) hosted Android emulators, iOS simulators, and real devices for the mobile engine, and hosted Chrome and Edge for the web engine. | | [`@e2e-dev/browserstack`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@e2e-dev/browserstack) | BrowserStack App Automate real Android and iOS devices for the mobile engine. | | [`@e2e-dev/limrun`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@e2e-dev/limrun) | Limrun hosted iOS simulators and Android emulators for mobile tests. | | [`@e2e-dev/eas`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@e2e-dev/eas) | Expo Simulators hosted iOS simulators and Android emulators for the mobile engine. | | [`@e2e-dev/github`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@e2e-dev/github) | Reporter that posts results as a pull request comment. | ## Documentation [e2e.com/docs](https://e2e.com/docs). The `e2e` package ships every page, so coding agents can read them offline in `node_modules/e2e/docs`. ## Join us Join us in changing how software gets tested. [We are hiring.](https://e2e.com/careers?utm_source=e2e&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=readme_hiring) Questions? Ask on [Discord](https://tester.army/discord). Issues are for bugs and feature requests. Want to hack on e2e? See [Contributing](./CONTRIBUTING.md). We prefer an issue or a Discord discussion before a pull request. ## Security Please don't open public issues for security vulnerabilities. Follow [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md) and report them to [security@e2e.com](mailto:security@e2e.com). ## Telemetry The CLI sends anonymous usage data, such as which commands and engines run and where runs fail, but no test content, app content, or credentials. Opt out with `npx e2e telemetry disable` or `E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1`. [Telemetry](https://e2e.com/docs/telemetry) lists every field. ## Status > [!NOTE] > e2e is in active development on the way to 1.0. APIs and config can still > change between minor releases.

name: ds-harness-remote
description: 基于 DeepSeek Harness 插件机制构建的远程访问方案，通过低延迟、端到端加密的 P2P 网络，支持使用 PC、移动端 和 Web 随时访问本地设备上的DSH 、CodeX、Cursor、Claude Code等工作区。 (Built on DeepSeek Harness plugins, this low-latency, end-to-end encrypted P2P solution lets PC, mobile, and web clients access local DSH, Codex, Cursor, and Claude Code workspaces.)
readme_content:
English  ·  中文  ·  日本語  ·  Documentation  ·  Web  ·  Android  ·  iOS

Self-hosting  ·  npm  · 

## Connect once. Ready whenever you are. Continue using your DeepSeek Harness instance from a phone, computer, or browser. Return to the same Harness session from whichever device is with you. Harness keeps running on your work computer, with the same workspaces, tools, and project setup. DS Harness Remote is simply another window into that environment. The DeepSeek Harness desktop edition is supported. Install the latest release: `ds-harness-remote@0.6.3` ## Features - Access your local Harness instance remotely from the web, a PC, or a mobile device: DSH first, with Codex, Cursor, and Antigravity support too. - DeepSeek Harness Desktop is ready to use after installation, with its native interface and no separate desktop conversation UI. - Create workspaces, configure models, and switch conversation models with the same smooth workflow as local use. - No public listening port or public IP is required on the Harness Host. Connect from anywhere with internet access over a bidirectional end-to-end encrypted channel. - Prefer P2P connections, use TURN relay nodes worldwide, and fall back to multiple Server Relays when needed. - Access workspace files, read-only previews, remote terminals, and authorized local development-service previews through the native Harness sidebar. - Remote Tool context injection supports Host and workspace discovery, Harness session creation and management, history reading, waiting for execution, interruption requests, and authorized file transfers. [Details](packages/plugin/README.md#remote-agent-tools). - Alongside DeepSeek Harness, access native workspaces for Codex, Cursor, Google Antigravity, Pi, OpenCode, Claude Code, Hermes Agent, and other tools through ACP integrations, with remote file browsing and terminals. - Clients are available across Android, iOS, Web, and native DSH. - Multiple clients can connect to the same Harness Host simultaneously, with RPC calls and streams isolated per connection. ## Contents - [Connect once. Ready whenever you are](#connect-once-ready-whenever-you-are) - [Features](#features) - [Supported clients](#supported-clients) - [Install](#install) - [Quick start](#quick-start) - [Screenshots](#screenshots) - [How it works](#how-it-works) - [Experimental ACP workspaces](#experimental-acp-workspaces) - [End-to-end encryption](#end-to-end-encryption) - [Network and transport](#network-and-transport) - [Security](#security) - [FAQ](#faq) - [Documentation](#documentation) - [Links](#links) - [Star History](#star-history) - [Project status and trademarks](#project-status-and-trademarks) - [License](#license) ## Supported clients | Client | Form | Status | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | DSH Desktop plugin | Remote sidebar | Supported | Install `ds-harness-remote@0.6.3`; this computer can also be the Host | | Web | Browser page | Supported | Open [https://dsh.r2049.cn](https://dsh.r2049.cn); reuses the native Harness interface | | Android | Native app | Supported | Download the APK from [Releases](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote/releases/latest); see the [Android guide](apps/android/README.md) | | DSH Go | A standout app by ccch1mneyyy | Supported | See [ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go: an Android client for DeepSeek Harness. Run it directly on your phone or control DSH on your computer remotely.](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go) | | iOS | TestFlight beta | Beta | Not publicly released; see [issue #20](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote/issues/20) | | Browser extension | Chrome | Entry point only | Exchanges an already signed-in Web authorization for a separate device credential, lists online Hosts and opens the same-origin Remote Web; it does not host a conversation UI | | dsh-TUI | Terminal-only CLI | Planned | Integration is not part of this release and returns in a later version; the installer never creates a Web service for it automatically | | Linux | Cloud server | Supported | Sign in on the [official website](https://dsh.r2049.cn/) for unattended installation with a single command and no configuration. | Several clients can connect to the same Host at once; RPC calls and streams are isolated per connection. ## Install ### DeepSeek Harness Desktop support Open **Extensions / Plugin management** in DeepSeek Harness Desktop, choose installation from npm, and enter this package: `ds-harness-remote@0.6.3` Restart Desktop afterward. Its official `dsh` launcher can also install the pinned package with `dsh plugin --profile desktop add -w ds-harness-remote@0.6.3`. On DSH 0.2.2+, npm installations support version checks and updates in Plugin management, with an attempt to restore the previous version if hot updating fails. GitHub and local link installations must switch to npm first; see [online updates](docs/installation.md#online-updates-in-dsh-plugin-management). ### Linux one-command installation Visit [https://dsh.r2049.cn](https://dsh.r2049.cn/), sign in, and obtain an installation authorization code to install with one command. ### Native Android client Keep conversations connected across multiple workspaces at once, and use **Bot mode**, powered by [Fei2411/DS-Bot](https://github.com/Fei2411/DS-Bot). Download the latest APK from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote/releases/latest), and sign in to the same account to see your Hosts. ## DSH Go — DeepSeek Harness in your pocket: run it locally on your phone or control your computer remotely. [ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go) has built-in support for the ds-harness-remote protocol. You can run DeepSeek Harness locally on your phone or connect to your computer remotely. After installing the ds-harness-remote plugin in DSH Go on your phone, you can also connect to the phone’s DSH from your computer or the web and use Mobile Use seamlessly. ### iOS client - [Join the beta](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote/issues/20) ## Quick start 1. Open **Remote** from the DeepSeek Harness sidebar. 2. Choose Zhihu, GitHub, or Google authorization, or sign in with an account and password. Account registration requires an invitation code; email the repository author to request one. 3. On another device, install the same plugin in DeepSeek Harness and sign in as described in steps 1–2. Alternatively, use Remote Web, iOS, Android, or DSH Go directly without installing a plugin. 4. Select an online Host, then choose an existing workspace or browse remote directories to open one. By default, Remote uses this project's hosted Server at [https://dsh.r2049.cn](https://dsh.r2049.cn). For self-hosting, use the repository's [minimal Server](apps/server/README.md). The current version includes WebRTC LAN/P2P/TURN coordination (TURN requires your own coturn deployment) and an encrypted Relay Server, but does not provide the full hosted Remote Web experience. ## Screenshots ### Desktop On another computer, select an online Host and open its workspace. The workspace opens in the native Harness interface, with the active Host and encrypted connection status in the header.

To prevent this computer from controlling other Hosts, open the Host list at [https://dsh.r2049.cn/](https://dsh.r2049.cn/) and enable **Controlled only**. This device will no longer see other devices under your account, while Web and other clients can still connect to it remotely. ### Android Use text or image prompts, switch models, and access supported workspace files and terminals. The interface follows the system language and supports English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Spanish, German, and French. In language settings, tap “More ...” to show all languages. See the [Android guide](apps/android/README.md) for details.

Mobile Settings includes a global **Compact conversations** switch, off by default and applied when a conversation is next opened. Supporting Hosts reduce historical tool details while preserving messages and tool status. Turn the setting off and reopen the conversation to load full history. ## How it works ```text DSH Desktop / Remote Web / Android ↔ authenticated, end-to-end encrypted channel Remote Plugin on the Host ↔ supported Harness or optional Codex workspace support Harness sessions/workspaces or Codex projects ``` The Harness Host does not need a public listening port. Connect from anywhere with internet access over ds-harness-remote’s bidirectional end-to-end encrypted channel. The client switches to the selected Host’s native Harness API, keeping the original workspaces, tools, and permission flows on that computer. You can also edit Harness and plugin settings on the remote host. Available options depend on which settings Harness and each plugin expose through the official settings API. ## Experimental ACP workspaces The Host runs local ACP-capable Agents and forwards prompts, streamed replies, and approvals through ds-harness-remote. Each Agent keeps its own workspaces and sessions; only session translation for DSH is performed, without writing to Harness storage. Supported backends: - **Codex** — connects through App Server, using the shared workspace entry. - **Cursor** — connects through the CLI's ACP interface. - **Antigravity (AGY)** — connects through an adapter for its stream-json CLI. - **Pi Agent (experimental)** — automatically detected after installing and configuring Pi and `pi-acp`; can be disabled in settings. Tools run with Host-user permissions, without per-tool confirmation by default. - **OpenCode** — connects through `opencode acp`, with workspaces and history. Session archiving requires a build with the authenticated API; unarchive is not yet available. - **Claude** — connects through a locally authorized `claude-agent-acp`; enable it in settings. Supports text and approvals; images are not yet supported. - **Hermes** — connects through `hermes acp`; enable it in settings. Supports text, images, streamed output, approvals, and model selection. Claude and Hermes also support direct file and terminal access, subject to the Host's workspace boundaries and terminal settings. Setup and adapter development: [Agent workspace integration guide](docs/acp-integration.md). Model selection for Cursor, Claude, Hermes, Pi, OpenCode, and AGY on Desktop/Android uses the Host's actual model catalog as determined by the Agent’s ACP interface. Reasoning effort optio

readme_content:
**Open-source AI teammates, working alongside your team in Slack, Teams, Discord, Telegram and Mattermost. Self-host it, with any agent and any model.** [![Website](https://img.shields.io/badge/website-switchagents.ai-FF895E)](https://www.switchagents.ai/) [![Product Hunt](https://img.shields.io/badge/Product%20Hunt-%231%20Product%20of%20the%20Day-FF6154?logo=producthunt&logoColor=white)](https://www.producthunt.com/products/switch-11?launch=switch-14) [![License: Apache 2.0 + Commons Clause](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0%20%2B%20Commons%20Clause-blue)](LICENSE) [![Documentation](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-read-FF895E)](https://docs.switchagents.ai/switch-rooms/getting-started) [![PRs welcome](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-brightgreen)](CONTRIBUTING.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/sandbox-quantum/switch?label=release&color=FF895E)](https://github.com/sandbox-quantum/switch/releases) [![CI](https://github.com/sandbox-quantum/switch/actions/workflows/pr-ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/sandbox-quantum/switch/actions/workflows/pr-ci.yml) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-join%20the%20community-5865F2?logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.com/invite/E6a2Jnb6G)
More than a single AI bot you ask questions to: Switch turns each channel into a room where your team and everyone's AI teammates work together, with shared context. - 💬 **Each channel becomes a room for people and agents**. Your agents join the conversation in Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord, Telegram and Mattermost, and everyone works from the same conversation, decisions and documents. Nobody has to learn a new tool or move anywhere. - 🌍 **Any agent, any model, any provider**. Your Claude Code agent on your laptop, a teammate's Codex agent on theirs, a LangChain agent on your servers. If it speaks the protocol, it can join. - 🧩 **AI teammates, not just bots**. Give each agent a role, instructions and tools (Google Workspace, Jira, GitHub), and link rooms the way your team works. Context moves with the work, and an agent only sees the rooms it belongs to. - 🏠 **Self-hosted, and the context is yours**. Run Switch on your own servers. Your team's context stays with your company, so you can change agents, models or vendors at any time without losing it. - 🛡️ **Run your team with confidence**. Decide who can talk to which agent, and in which rooms. Guardrails and cost reporting come with [Switch Trust](https://www.switchagents.ai/trust) and [Switch ROI](https://www.switchagents.ai/roi). ## Get started in two steps 1. **Install Switch Console**, the desktop app, for your platform. 2. **Open it and talk to switch-buddy**, your own assistant in Switch. Tell it what you want: it creates your first agents and channels, helps you connect the chat app your team uses, and answers anything about Switch. | Platform | Install | | --- | --- | | macOS | [Apple Silicon](https://github.com/sandbox-quantum/switch/releases/latest/download/switch-console-arm64.dmg) · [Intel](https://github.com/sandbox-quantum/switch/releases/latest/download/switch-console-x64.dmg) | | Windows | [Installer](https://github.com/sandbox-quantum/switch/releases/latest/download/switch-console-x64.exe) | | Linux x64 | [AppImage](https://github.com/sandbox-quantum/switch/releases/latest/download/switch-console-x86_64.AppImage) · [DEB](https://github.com/sandbox-quantum/switch/releases/latest/download/switch-console-amd64.deb) | | Linux ARM64 | [AppImage](https://github.com/sandbox-quantum/switch/releases/latest/download/switch-console-arm64.AppImage) · [DEB](https://github.com/sandbox-quantum/switch/releases/latest/download/switch-console-arm64.deb) | See the [latest release](https://github.com/sandbox-quantum/switch/releases/latest) for all desktop builds. ## Watch it work The same incident, in the apps teams already use. Someone reports checkout failing, an agent opens an incident channel, pulls the error rate and finds the deploy behind it — with a second agent doing the charting. Under a minute each, no narration.
Slack https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d7db7859-c1e0-4d2c-9675-1cc3966a1bfd
Discord https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e114cf81-41b0-4cce-a06f-5e78830bf99d
Mattermost https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/51918de4-4283-4717-bdfa-d63f9da8eae1
## Why Switch Your agents can do far more for your team than answer one question at a time. Switch is what unlocks it. You do not have to start big. Each level builds on the one before it, the first works on day one, and each one gets more out of your agents than the last.
⚡ Level 1. Your everyday agents move into your messaging app. - Work on a feature with a colleague and your Claude Code agent, all in one channel. - Pull a colleague in to review what you and your agent have been doing. The whole trail is already there, nothing to paste or re-explain. - Stand up a Codex agent that knows one slice of the system well, and let any colleague ask it questions directly. - Open a channel for a feature and put the people and agents that feature needs into it.
⚡⚡ Level 2. You start encoding how the work runs. - A bootstrap channel where anyone asks a manager agent to start a piece of work. It opens the channel, brings in the right people and agents, attaches the context they need, and gets it moving. - A feature request channel where an agent triages what comes in, asks the questions you would have asked, and files it in Jira, Confluence or Notion. - A bug report channel where an agent reproduces what it can, collects the logs and versions, and either files the ticket or tells the reporter what is still missing.
⚡⚡⚡ Level 3. Your team runs on Switch. - Someone reports a bug, the triage agent reproduces it, a coding agent fixes it in a channel of its own, a person reviews the fix, and the deployment agent puts it on the test environment. - The triage agent files a feature request, a coding agent builds it in a work channel with the ticket and design already in it, and whoever asked for it signs it off. - An alert lands in the on-call channel, whoever holds the role that week picks it up, it goes down the same path as any bug, and an agent writes up what happened into the team's knowledge. - Someone asks a question in the support channel, the support agent answers from the runbooks, and when a runbook turns out to be wrong that agent corrects it in the channel that owns it.
⚡⚡⚡⚡ Level 4. Your company runs on Switch. Every person, team and department works alongside agents, and work crosses between them the same way it crosses between channels.
## What Switch is not Most tools in this space want to become the place your team works. Switch does not replace the stack you already have. It connects it. - ❌ **Not a messaging app**. Slack, Teams, Discord, Telegram and Mattermost stay where they are. Switch brings your agents and the workflows you define into them, so nobody has to move. - ❌ **Not an agent provider**. Switch ships no agents and no models. You keep Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or whatever you already run, and Switch is what lets them work with your team. - ❌ **Not a black box self-service platform**. Switch's code is here for everyone to see and contribute to. It is designed to be self-hostable and for your data to stay where it is. Getting humans and agents to work as one team is the part nobody has solved yet. That is where our effort goes, rather than into rebuilding chat apps and coding agents that already work well. ## Docs ### Let an agent walk you through them Rather than working through the documentation yourself, connect an agent to it and have it take you through the steps, answering your questions as they come up. The docs are served over MCP at https://docs.switchagents.ai/mcp. Connect your agent to the MCP server and ask it: > How do I get started with Switch? #### Claude Code Run the following command in a terminal. ```bash claude mcp add switch-docs --transport http https://docs.switchagents.ai/mcp ``` #### OpenAI Codex CLI Run the following command in a terminal. ```bash codex mcp add switch-docs --url https://docs.switchagents.ai/mcp ``` #### OpenCode Run the following command in a terminal. ```bash opencode mcp add ``` Then follow the procedure and provide `https://docs.switchagents.ai/mcp` as the MCP server URL. ### Read them yourself - [Getting started](https://docs.switchagents.ai/switch-rooms/getting-started): from your first agent to your first channel. - [Hosting remotely](https://docs.switchagents.ai/switch-rooms/deploy/host-remotely): deploy Switch for your team. ## Telemetry Switch Console collects anonymous usage analytics to help us understand how the app is used and improve it. Telemetry is **opt-out** — it is on by default, you are told about it on first run, and one toggle turns it off. What we collect: | Data | Example | Purpose | | --- | --- | --- | | Event name | `session_started`, `room_created` | Understand which features are used | | App version | `0.9.14` | Track adoption of new releases | | Release channel | `stable` | Separate pre-release from released usage | | Operating system | `darwin`, `23.6.0` | Prioritise platform support | | Agent provider | `claude`, `codex` | Understand which agents people run | | Outcome and error code | `failure`, `docker_daemon_down` | Prioritise bug fixes | | Counts and flags | `agent_count: 3`, `has_initial_prompt: true` | Size features without seeing content | | Anonymous client ID | `3f2a9c41-…` (random UUID) | Count unique installations | Every field is drawn from a fixed vocabulary of enumerated values, numbers and booleans — free text cannot be transmitted. **What we never collect:** source code, prompts, file paths, working directories, repository or project names, room or agent names, server URLs or hostnames, usernames, emails, API keys or credentials, model outputs, search queries, error messages or stack traces, IP addresses, or any personally identifiable information.
